newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish PM confident of winning censure vote.
newsitem.headline: Turkish PM confident of winning censure vote.

text.p: Turkey's Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan said on Tuesday he was confident of surviving an opposition censure motion designed to topple his Islamist-led government.

"Our government will see its vote of confidence renewed as the censure motion is thrown out once again," Erbakan told reporters. "So, God willing, this censure motion will give rise to a lovely day for us."

Parliament speaker Mustafa Kalemli said earlier that the house would on Tuesday begin a preliminary debate on the censure motion -- which criticises the government for moving away from the country's secular tradition.
The government, which has 280 seats in the 550-seat parliament, has survived three other censure motions against it. A censure motion is effectively a vote of no-confidence against the government.

If parliament votes on Tuesday to go ahead with the censure motion, it will hold a final vote on Saturday. But according Turkish parliamentary tradition the government would resign if it loses Tuesday's vote.
